summary:
MELIORA is an astronaut health-monitoring system developed to support crew wellbeing and medical oversight during space missions. We built an integrated platform that collects physiological measurements, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation and body temperature, alongside crew wellness and symptom reports. It analyses health trends against individual baselines, generates explainable clinical assessments, and provides prioritized alerts for flight surgeons. Its offline store-and-forward synchronization mechanism ensures that health data can be securely retained and synchronized even during communication blackouts or Loss-of-Signal (LOS) periods.

MELIORA addresses the challenge of maintaining reliable astronaut health monitoring in demanding spaceflight environments, where communication delays, limited medical resources and changing physiological conditions complicate healthcare delivery. By combining continuous health-data management, deterministic clinical assessment, secure data handling and an interactive mission dashboard, it supports informed medical review and timely intervention. Its importance lies in strengthening astronaut health awareness, improving operational resilience and contributing to safer, more sustainable human space exploration.
details:
MELIORA is an astronaut health-monitoring system designed to support crew wellbeing during space missions, including periods of intermittent communication with Earth. It collects physiological data such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and body temperature, alongside self-reported wellness and symptom check-ins. The system analyses longitudinal trends, compares readings against individual baselines, and uses explainable, deterministic clinical rules to generate assessments and prioritized alerts. Its store-and-forward synchronization mechanism ensures reliable data transfer during Loss-of-Signal (LOS) periods.

MELIORA benefits astronauts and flight surgeons through centralized health monitoring, traceable assessments, early identification of potential concerns, and resilient data management. Its intended impact is to improve crew health awareness, support timely medical review, and strengthen healthcare operations in space.

The project uses Python 3.12, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, Next.js, React, TypeScript, Three.js, and Recharts. Its creativity lies in combining aerospace-inspired visualization, interactive 3D spacecraft graphics, longitudinal health analytics, and offline resilience. Key considerations included data security, clinical explainability, human oversight, communication delays, and the safety of astronauts in demanding spaceflight environments.
